{{Short description|American mechanical engineer}}
'''Steven L. Brunton''' is an American mechanical engineer and applied mathematician. He is the Boeing Professor of AI & Data-Driven Engineering at the [[University of Washington]], where his research focuses on applying machine learning to dynamical systems, fluid mechanics, and control theory.<ref name="auto">{{cite web | title=Steve Brunton | url=https://www.me.washington.edu/facultyfinder/steve-brunton }}</ref> He serves as Director of NSF AI Institute in Dynamic Systems, the AI Center for Dynamics and Control (ACDC), and the AI for Engineering Education Institute (AIEEI).<ref>{{cite web | title=ME Professor Steve Brunton elected American Physical Society Fellow | date=3 October 2024 | url=https://www.me.washington.edu/news/article/2024-10-04/steve-brunton-elected-aps-fellow }}</ref>

== Education and career ==
Brunton earned a Bachelor of Science degree in mathematics, with a minor in control and dynamical systems, from the [[California Institute of Technology]] in 2006.<ref>{{cite web
 |title=California Institute of Technology Commencement Program 2006|url=https://campuspubs.library.caltech.edu/2144/1/Commencement_2006.pdf
 |website=Caltech Campus Publications
 |year=2006
 |format=PDF
 |access-date=2026-02-20
}}</ref> He completed his Ph.D. in mechanical and aerospace engineering at [[Princeton University]] in 2012.<ref>{{cite web
 |title=Steven L. Brunton – Princeton University Archives
 |url=https://findingaids.princeton.edu/catalog/AC105-05_c12390/
 |website=Princeton University
 |access-date=2026-02-20
}}</ref> Following a postdoctoral position in applied mathematics at the University of Washington, he joined the faculty there in 2014, where he is now a full professor.<ref name="auto"/>

== Research ==
Brunton’s research combines methods from applied mathematics, machine learning, and physics-based modeling to analyze and control complex systems. His work spans model discovery, reduced-order modeling, sparse sensing, and control, with applications in fluid dynamics, aerospace engineering, energy systems, and neuroscience.<ref name="Brunton2020ARFM">S. L. Brunton, B. R. Noack, and P. Koumoutsakos. "Machine Learning for Fluid Mechanics." ''Annual Review of Fluid Mechanics'', 52:477–508, 2020. [https://doi.org/10.1146/annurev-fluid-010719-060214 doi:10.1146/annurev-fluid-010719-060214]</ref>

Brunton is noted for developing the [[Sparse identification of non-linear dynamics]] (SINDy) algorithm<ref name="Brunton2016PNAS">S. L. Brunton, J. L. Proctor, and J. N. Kutz. "Discovering governing equations from data: Sparse identification of nonlinear dynamical systems." ''Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences'', 113(15):3932–3937, 2016. [https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1517384113 doi:10.1073/pnas.1517384113]</ref> and for his contributions to data-driven modeling in engineering and the physical sciences, specifically in fluid dynamics.<ref name="Brunton2020ARFM" />

== Books ==

* Kutz, J. N., Brunton, S. L., Brunton, B. W., & Proctor, J. L. ''[https://epubs.siam.org/doi/book/10.1137/1.9781611974508 Dynamic Mode Decomposition: Data-Driven Modeling of Complex Systems].'' Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics (SIAM), 2016. ISBN 978-1-61197-449-2.
* Duriez, T., Brunton, S. L., & Noack, B. R. ''[https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-319-40624-4 Machine Learning Control: Taming Nonlinear Dynamics and Turbulence].'' Springer, 2017. DOI: 10.1007/978-3-319-40624-4.
* Mendez, M. A., Ianiro, A., Noack, B. R., & Brunton, S. L. (Eds.). ''[https://doi.org/10.1017/9781108896214 Data-Driven Fluid Mechanics: Combining First Principles and Machine Learning].'' Cambridge University Press, 2023. DOI: 10.1017/9781108896214.
